solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See 5
Not so much a time to raise hanging threads

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the letters means reading them from the bottom upwards

parts.note: not so much is less
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A suggestion to wait less before lifting some dangling strands.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string LESS A T is turned upwards to give TASSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassel is a decorative tuft of loose threads or cords knotted at one end and left dangling.

clue.text: Oresteia somehow packs in 100 mysterious items

indicators.note: to pack something in is to stuff it inside, so one piece goes within the other
somehow says the letters arrive by some unstated route, so their order is not fixed

parts.note: taken as written: Aeschylus's trilogy of Greek tragedies
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Aeschylus's trilogy somehow crams in a hundred arcane objects.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of Oresteia are rearranged and C is slipped in just before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure items or facts understood only by a select few, hence mysterious things.

clue.text: Dwarf very soft grass covers

indicators.note: what covers something lies over and around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: hay is dried grass
pianissimo, the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A tiny figure is hidden by very soft grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwarf' looks like a verb meaning to overshadow; it is one of the Seven Dwarfs of Snow White.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is the name of one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White.

clue.text: Old Syrian people hospitalised?

indicators.note: hospitalised means placed inside a medical facility, so the word for people goes inside a short word for one

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital
a race is a people

explanation.surface: A question about whether some ancient Syrians had been admitted to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hospitalised' does double duty: it supplies SAN and says the people go inside it; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the old name for an Arab or Muslim of Syria and the wider Levant, especially in Crusader times.

clue.text: Corrupt Hughes to get VIP pass

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoiled and bent out of its proper form, so the words are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: A bent official named Hughes is bribed to hand out a VIP pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder; 'pass' looks like a ticket to go with the VIP, but it is the verb meaning to die.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass is a euphemism for dying, and the idiom for dying or ceasing to function is exactly this phrase.

clue.text: Called into question, force endlessly hurt

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to impel is to force
ached means hurt

explanation.surface: Someone's conduct was challenged after force caused unending pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach a witness or a statement is to challenge its credibility, to call it into question.

clue.text: Weapon up before court causing bleed

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom towards the top

parts.note: an axe is a weapon
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A weapon raised in a courtroom leads to bloodshed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bleed' suggests wounds from the weapon; here it means to drain someone of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact money is to extort it, just as to bleed someone is to squeeze them for cash.

clue.text: Coward Oscar in place with Scottish links

indicators.note: in places the first named letter inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Royal Troon is an Open Championship golf links in Ayrshire, Scotland

explanation.surface: A cowardly Oscar settles in a spot near Scottish golf courses.
explanation.walkthrough: Links are seaside golf courses; Troon on the Ayrshire coast hosts the Open.
explanation.definitionFit: A poltroon is an old-fashioned word for an utter coward.

clue.text: Dramatist succeeded with Best Shakespearean Cat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
top means best
pard is an old word for a leopard, used by Shakespeare ('bearded like the pard')

explanation.surface: A playwright triumphed with the finest feline character from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Stoppard is the British playwright of Arcadia and Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Stoppard is a celebrated modern playwright, so he fits a clue asking for a writer of plays.

clue.text: Student bends over in uncontrolled expansion

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: L for learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
warps means bends out of shape

explanation.surface: A student leans over in a picture of unchecked growth.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces together are read backwards, not just the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprawl, as in urban sprawl, is the untidy, unplanned spreading of something over a wide area.

clue.text: Manipulative 13 in 16, one needing a wee …

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
a go can mean a visit to the toilet, so to wee is to go

explanation.surface: A scheming figure in a play desperately needs the toilet, the ellipsis trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is CHARACTER and 16 is OTHELLO, so the definition reads 'manipulative character in Othello'. The ellipsis links the surface to the sword clue that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming ensign who manipulates Othello into jealousy in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Hostile yankee served with nut and mutton

definitions.note: the answer is a noun used attributively, as in enemy territory

parts.note: printers call an en space a nut
printers call an em space a mutton
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An unfriendly American is served a dish of nuts and mutton.
explanation.walkthrough: Typesetters said 'nut' and 'mutton' to tell the en and em spaces apart by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemy works as an adjective in phrases like enemy fire, describing what belongs to a hostile force.

clue.text: Describe old make-up case

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an archaic verb, to describe or portray
second meaning: a person's nature or disposition
third meaning: an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: Telling someone to describe a worn-out cosmetics case.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: 'old' marks the first sense as archaic, and 'make-up' is temperament, not cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: The word once served as a verb for portraying; it also names one's nature, and an oddball is called a real one.

clue.text: In moonlight this poet wrestles with hog

indicators.note: wrestling bodies twist and tangle, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the poet together with the hog make up the given word, so taking one away leaves the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: By moonlight, a poet grapples with a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the poet plus HOG together rearrange into MOONLIGHT, so take HOG's letters out and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton was the English poet who wrote Paradise Lost.

clue.text: … sword pushed in so far? Absolutely!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a blade driven in until the handle stops it
second meaning: completely, to the utmost

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the previous clue's Iago, who stabs his wife in Othello. The question mark flags the literal reading of an idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The hilt is a sword's handle, so a blade buried that far is in fully, and the idiom means completely.

clue.text: Soldier of misfortune to back suffering love

indicators.note: going back means the short word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
hell is great suffering
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A down-on-his-luck mercenary turns back to his suffering love.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition twists 'soldier of fortune'; Othello is a general whose story ends in tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's Moorish general, a military man brought to ruin, hence one of misfortune.

clue.text: Power in maths Mr Goliath repurposed

indicators.note: repurposed means adapted for a different use, so the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The giant Goliath finds a new role as a mathematical force.
explanation.definitionFit: A logarithm is the exponent, or power, to which a base must be raised to produce a given number.

clue.text: Plague's long story the same Roman interrupts

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative
idem is Latin for the same

explanation.surface: The tale of a plague is a lengthy saga, though the same Roman keeps breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' signals that the word for 'the same' is wanted in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of disease, which is what a plague is.

clue.text: Go on piano — make short hard sounds

parts.note: P is the musical marking for piano, softly
to rattle is to make a rapid series of short knocking sounds

explanation.surface: Instructions to play the piano percussively, hammering out staccato noises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' looks like encouragement to the pianist; it means to talk at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To prattle is to chatter on foolishly, and to go on is to talk tediously at length.

clue.text: Lover bowed runs into Dawn

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

parts.note: Eos is the Greek goddess of the dawn
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A suitor bows and then hurries towards a woman named Dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowed' looks like the suitor bending; it means carrying a bow, as the love god does.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, always pictured armed with a bow and arrows.

clue.text: Later life of good ale a round missed badly

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so the letters end up out of order
something missed is left out, so a letter drops from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
a round letter, shaped like a ring; this one is removed

explanation.surface: In retirement, a round at the pub is missed and the good ale poorly served.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Os in GOOD is dropped before the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Old age is the final stretch of a lifetime, the later years of life.

clue.text: Air on with AC needing fix — something blown

indicators.note: something needing a fix is broken, so these letters must be put right in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Air conditioning that is switched on and needs repair has blown a fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown' suggests a broken fuse in the air-con; it means played by blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, so it is played by blowing into it.

clue.text: Centaur Club supports check

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports another piece sits beneath it, fixing the order

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club backs up a cheque, or a mythical horse-man.
explanation.walkthrough: Chiron was the wise centaur who tutored Achilles in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiron is the best-known centaur of Greek mythology, a teacher of heroes.

clue.text: 16's victim some French fiend initially assailed

parts.note: des is French for some
a demon is a fiend

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it qualifies

parts.note: the first letter of assailed

explanation.surface: Othello's victim was attacked by something like a French devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is OTHELLO, whose wife he smothers in jealous rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona is Othello's wife, whom he murders in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Say street fight isn't very good?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a brawl, of which a street fight is one example
second meaning: read as ''...', slang for being of poor quality

explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' flags a definition by example. The second half is a cheeky split reading, with 'it' understood: it's crap.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is an informal word for a brawl, and run together, "'s crap" says the thing is rubbish.

clue.text: 16's victim Walk for days early in the year
Pipe connects with Eastern State

parts.note: a main is a principal pipe for water or gas
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A pipe links up with an eastern state.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in the far north-east of New England.

clue.text: Sheepish male returned drink allowance

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: An embarrassed man sends back his drinks quota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' reads as embarrassed; it means of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is an amount allowed beyond what is needed, as in a margin for error.

clue.text: Such as Emilia to 23 around home? Unlucky

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: Emilia is a fellow woman and companion to Desdemona, loosely a sister to her
in means at home

explanation.surface: Is Emilia close to Desdemona around the house? Bad luck if so.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is DESDEMONA; Emilia is Iago's wife and Desdemona's attendant, so 'sister' is a loose fit, as the blog's commenters noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister once meant left-handed and so ill-omened, hence threatening bad luck.

clue.text: Writer brings a lobster-trap into church

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the pieces go within the word for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written
a lobster pot is the trap for catching lobsters

explanation.surface: An author carries a lobster trap into a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was the American author of In Cold Blood and Breakfast at Tiffany's.

clue.text: Northerner's distressed damsel with a knight

indicators.note: distressed means troubled or knocked about, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A northern damsel in distress is rescued by a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dales are the valleys of Yorkshire in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalesman is a man from the Yorkshire Dales, so a native of the north of England.
